action.description: Which operation to perform — pass its matching params object below (e.g. action: "fetch-attachments" pairs with fetchAttachments: {...}).

messageId.description: Gmail message ID from fetch-conversation output (shown as "Message ID:" on each email). Required to fetch attachments.

attachmentId.description: Optional attachment ID from the attachments list. When omitted, fetches and extracts text from all attachments on the message.

write_to_file.description: When true, writes large extracted content to a TASK_BUFFER doc instead of returning inline.

targetUserId.description: Read ANOTHER user instead of yourself. Omit for your own sent email, which is almost always what you want. This returns verbatim drafted and sent message bodies, so a cross-user read is refused even for an admin of the target's own organization.

userId.description: DEPRECATED alias for targetUserId, kept so existing callers keep working. It is NOT the authenticated identity: it names whose sent email to read, and goes through the same authorization gate.

maxSimilarity.description: Filter to emails where the user changed the draft significantly. 0.6 = user rewrote >40% of the content. Use this to find examples of what the agent gets wrong.

direction.description: Filter by direction. Use "outbound" for emails the user sent.

hasAttachments.description: When true, only return emails that have file attachments.

fromEmail.description: Filter by sender email address (exact match).

subjectContains.description: Filter emails whose subject contains this string (case-insensitive).

snippetContains.description: Filter emails whose body snippet contains this string (case-insensitive). Useful for finding emails that mention a specific attachment by name, e.g. "explainer deck", "pitch deck", "qsbs-stacking".

dateFrom.description: ISO 8601 date — only include emails on or after this date.

dateTo.description: ISO 8601 date — only include emails on or before this date.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return.

query.description: Gmail search query — full Gmail search syntax (e.g. "from:jane@acme.com newer_than:30d has:attachment subject:intro"). Searches the user's LIVE mailbox, not Cedar's synced store. Returns thread ids + subject/from/snippet previews.

folder.description: Gmail folder to scope the search to. Default "inbox".

threadId.description: Gmail thread id (from search-live). Reads the full thread LIVE from the mailbox.

user_request_summary.description: One sentence, in your own words: what the user actually asked you to do in this turn. Used only for Cedar's observability — it does not change what this tool does.

is_new_request.description: true on the FIRST Cedar tool call of a NEW user request; false when this call continues the same request you are already working on. Groups related calls into one activity thread.
